joint_histogram — IMGMETRICS information op

• Data kinds: image2d × image2d → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.joint_histogram(a, b, bins=64, data_range=None) (to call the implementation directly, import imgmetrics; imgmetrics.joint_histogram(a, b, bins=64, data_range=None); from the registry, opsimgmetrics.get("joint_histogram"))

Usage

Joint histogram of two images (the normalised joint probability).

The bin width is set from data_range -- if it were stretched per image by min/max, a uniformly dark picture and a uniformly bright picture would have the same mutual information.

Procedure: flatten the 2 images, take numpy.histogram2d with the same bin edges [lo, lo + data_range] for both (lo = the smaller of the 2 images' minima, divided into bins equal parts), and divide by the total count to get the joint probability.

• a, b: same shape (any dimensionality), finite. If the dtypes are not the same, give data_range explicitly (inference from mixed dtypes is rejected).

• bins: an integer of at least 2.

• data_range: automatic for integer dtypes (uint8 = 255 etc.); for float, only when in [0, 1] is it 1.0, otherwise it must be given explicitly.

• Return value: float64 of shape (bins, bins), summing to 1. Rows are bins of a, columns bins of b. Values above lo + data_range do not fall into any bin (they are not counted).

• Failure (MetricContractError): shapes differ / empty / non-finite / bins < 2 / 0 samples fall within the range.
